Habitat: Cultivated Landscape / Pathway border
Ecological Role: Ornamental flowering shrub/tree with broad, obovate glossy green leaves with blunt apices. Flowers provide nectar to pollinators like hawk moths.
Description: Evergreen tree/shrub known for glossy dark green obovate leaves with blunt tips and fragrant white flowers with yellow centers. Drought tolerant and highly attractive to pollinating sphinx/hawk moths.

Common Name: Tropical Hibiscus / China Rose & Red Hibiscus / Shoeblack Plant
Habitat: Garden hedge / Pathway border
Ecological Role: Widely planted ornamental shrub supporting local pollinators including butterflies, bees, and nectar-feeding birds (sunbirds). Crimson and multi-colored blooms feature prominent staminal columns.
Description: Evergreen flowering shrub with ovate serrated leaves and large solitary 5-petaled flowers with exerted staminal columns. Observed in multiple color cultivars (Tropical China Rose morph and Crimson Red Shoeblack morph) across campus pathways.
Survey Source: Survey Specimens 02 & 12 (Deduplicated single species with documented cultivars)

Habitat: Climbing vegetation / Ground cover
Ecological Role: Bipinnate vine that acts as ground cover and climbs nearby vegetation, providing shelter for small insects and berries consumed by wild birds.
Description: Perennial deciduous or semi-evergreen woody vine characterized by bipinnately compound leaves with serrated margins. Produces small berry clusters that serve as crucial food for campus avifauna.

Habitat: Open landscape / Architectural accent
Ecological Role: Distinctive silvery-blue, massive fan-shaped fronds. Serves as an ornamental accent tree and microhabitat for urban birds and insects. Falling leaves add organic biomass to soil.
Description: Noble solitary palm indigenous to Madagascar with a stout trunk topped by a massive spherical crown of steel-blue, costapalmate leaves. Provides elevated perches for predatory and passerine birds.

Habitat: Shaded understory / Courtyard
Ecological Role: Multi-stemmed, shade-tolerant palm with glossy palmate fronds, commonly cultivated in campus understory landscapes and indoor atriums. Provides dense lower-canopy cover.
Description: Densely clustering fan palm with slender bamboo-like stems covered in coarse brown fiber. The deeply divided palmate leaves create microhabitats for ground invertebrates.

Common Name: Sugar Date Palm / Wild Date Palm
Habitat: Open grounds / Semi-arid landscape
Ecological Role: Hardy native palm producing dense crowns of spiny pinnate leaves and small edible fruits that feed bats, birds, and bonnet macaques.
Description: Robust native palm reaching up to 15m in height, characterized by diamond-shaped leaf base scars on the trunk. Fruit clusters are vital seasonal food resources for campus wildlife.

Habitat: Ornamental garden bed / Wall trellis
Ecological Role: Evergreen sprawling shrub with large, vivid yellow funnel-shaped blooms. High ornamental value; supports long-tongued insect pollinators.
Description: Vigorous sprawling evergreen shrub with whorled glossy leathery leaves and trumpet-shaped golden-yellow flowers emitting a delicate fragrance.

Habitat: Sunny roadside margin / Open soil
Ecological Role: Serrated leaves with paired extrafloral nectaries at leaf bases that attract ants for biological protection; bright yellow diurnal flowers sustain diverse butterflies and bees.
Description: Erect perennial subshrub with deeply veined, dark green serrated leaves. Exhibits mutualistic interactions with native ants through nectar-secreting glands on petioles.

Habitat: Open quadrangle / Building surroundings
Ecological Role: Highly fragrant, five-petaled white flowers with a central yellow throat. Produces milky latex; pollinated primarily by nocturnal sphinx moths.
Description: Small deciduous tree with narrow elongated lanceolate leaves having distinct downward-curled margins. Flowers release intense fragrance in the evening.

Habitat: Landscaped courtyard / Open lawn
Ecological Role: Striking terminal inflorescence clusters of reddish-pink buds and fragrant blossoms, offering drought tolerance and architectural landscaping value.
Description: Deciduous tree with thick succulent branches and elliptic-oblong pointed leaves. Renowned for rich aromatic deep pink-red blossoms that bloom in terminal cymes.

Habitat: Moist soil border / Drainage margin
Ecological Role: Features elegant white star-shaped flowers with delicate spider-like petals radiating from a central cup. Thrives in moist soils and filters runoff water.
Description: Bulbous perennial herb with strap-like linear leaves and umbels of pure white spider-like blossoms. Roots stabilize soil along moist drainage contours.

Habitat: Trained on pergola / Garden trellis
Ecological Role: Drought-tolerant climbing woody shrub with vibrant magenta-pink petaloid bracts enclosing small tubular flowers. Provides dense nesting foliage for birds and abundant nectar for long-tongued butterflies and bees.
Description: Vigorous thorny evergreen shrub or woody climber featuring showy, paper-thin magenta bracts. Bracts shield delicate cream-white floral tubes adapted for pollinator visits.

Habitat: Moist soil / Grassy open ground
Ecological Role: Moisture-loving perennial herb producing slender spikes of delicate pink flowers. Helps stabilize moist soil and provides nectar to campus micro-pollinators.
Description: Herbaceous plant characterized by lanceolate leaves with ciliate ocreae and dense spicate racemes of pinkish-white flowers. Thrives in localized damp spots near open campus lawns.

Location: Central plaza beds, SSN Admin Block Road
Habitat: Clipped hedge, full sun to partial shade
Ecological Role: Compact evergreen shrub with dense corymbs of scarlet-red and pink tubular flowers. Long corolla tubes provide critical nectar resources for long-tongued butterflies, sunbirds, and honeybees.
Description: Dense flowering shrub with opposite, glossy leathery oblong leaves and terminal clusters of four-petaled scarlet or salmon-pink tubular flowers. Extensively cultivated as attractive boundary hedges.

Habitat: Potted planters, maintained ornamental beds
Ecological Role: Continuously blooming nectar plant bearing corymbs of 5-pointed star-shaped pink/magenta flowers. Consistently recorded as the most visited nectar source for butterflies and native bees on campus.
Description: Erect perennial with lanceolate veined leaves and terminal umbel-like cymes packed with star-shaped tubular flowers. Highly prized in campus pollinator gardens.

Location: Central plaza beds, SSN Admin Block Road
Habitat: Container soil & open garden beds, full sun
Ecological Role: Sun-loving composite flower with exposed central disc florets and bright pink/crimson ray petals. Easily accessible nectar and pollen sustain native bees, syrphid flies, and butterflies.
Description: Stiff, erect annual herb with opposite sessile leaves and solitary composite flower heads. Central disc florets provide accessible pollen rewards.

Location: Hostel garden pots, Gents Hostel Road
Habitat: Potted cultivation, partial shade
Ecological Role: Ornamental potted cultivar bearing multi-layered white-and-yellow double flower heads. Cultivated for student residence aesthetics.
Description: Bushy perennial with lobed aromatic foliage and pompon-like multi-petaled double floral heads. Densely packed ray florets offer structural microclimate in patio pots.

Location: Central plaza beds, SSN Admin Block Road
Habitat: Rough grassy margins beside maintained beds
Ecological Role: Feathery-foliaged annual herb with saucer-like lilac-pink ray florets surrounding a yellow disc. Readily self-seeds in open grassy verge habitats and attracts beneficial pollinators.
Description: Slender herbaceous annual with deeply divided pinnatisect leaves and terminal flower heads with delicate fluted ray petals radiating from a sunny yellow center.

Location: Central plaza beds, SSN Admin Block Road
Habitat: Shaded shrub beds beside paving
Ecological Role: Evergreen shrub bearing waxy pinwheel-shaped white flowers emitting a delicate fragrance at dusk. Sustains nocturnal moths and diurnal micro-insects.
Description: Glossy-leaved dichotomously branched evergreen shrub with milky sap and snow-white 5-petaled pinwheel flowers arranged in small cymes.

Location: Rough ground beside Bio-Medical Engineering block
Habitat: Disturbed open soil, roadside wasteland & leaf litter
Ecological Role: Hardy, multi-colored flowering shrub with inflorescences shifting from yellow to pink to orange. While ecologically invasive in forests, campus bushes act as an indispensable nectar magnet for butterflies.
Description: Perennial woody shrub with ovate scabrous leaves with toothed margins and compact umbilical head of tubular flowers in contrasting colors. Produces small dark drupes.

Habitat: Clipped hedge beside mown turf
Ecological Role: Bright chartreuse-foliaged shrub maintained as a formal boundary hedge. Serves as a vital lookout and thermoregulation perch for oriental garden lizards (*Calotes versicolor*).
Description: Sprawling woody shrub cultivated for its vibrant golden-green foliage. Provides dense shelter and perches along the perimeter of open lawn turf.

Habitat: Mown turf, open sun, sports fields
Ecological Role: Stoloniferous mat-forming perennial grass that stabilizes campus topsoil, resists foot traffic, and provides primary forage for herbivorous grasshoppers, seed bugs, and peafowl.
Description: Hardy prostrate grass with extensive rhizomes and stolons, greyish-green blades, and terminal digitately arranged flower spikes.

Habitat: Damp mown turf following monsoon rains
Ecological Role: Saprotrophic macrofungus whose subterranean mycelial network rapidly breaks down dead lawn grass roots and organic clippings, unlocking mineral nutrients back to the soil.
Description: Fruiting mushroom with a tall stalk and a broad convex cap covered in concentric brownish scales on a pale background. Appears gregariously in open lawns after heavy rainfall.

Habitat: Naturalised herb in cultivated garden borders
Ecological Role: Hardy perennial herb producing dense upright spikes of two-lipped violet-purple flowers with specialized floral oil glands that attract solitary pollinating bees.
Description: Bushy erect herb with narrow willow-like serrated leaves and terminal spikes crowded with purple snapdragon-like flowers emitting an apple-like scent.

Habitat: Ornamental lawn planting, full sun to partial shade
Ecological Role: Ancient gymnosperm dating back to the Mesozoic era, possessing nitrogen-fixing coralloid roots with symbiotic cyanobacteria. Provides high architectural landscape value.
Description: Slow-growing palm-like cycad featuring a thick shaggy trunk topped by a symmetrical rosette of stiff, glossy dark green pinnate leaves with revolute margins.

Common Name: Ruffled Fan Palm / Vanuatu Fan Palm
Habitat: Shaded indoor-outdoor courtyard planting
Ecological Role: Understory palm prized for magnificent undivided pleated circular fronds that channel rainwater down petioles to root zones.
Description: Stunning small solitary palm with erect slender trunk and large, undivided orbicular fan-shaped leaves with deeply pleated, notched margins.

Habitat: Shaded, moist gravel/soil planter
Ecological Role: Vibrant yellow-green architectural aroid capable of absorbing indoor atmospheric pollutants and thriving in low-light shaded planters.
Description: Stout rosette-forming tropical aroid displaying luminous chartreuse-gold ovate leaves supported by robust succulent orange-tinted petioles.

Habitat: Trailing over rocks and roadside embankments
Ecological Role: Native drought-hardy climber with fragrant star-shaped white flowers that attract nocturnal hawkmoths and diurnal butterflies. Foliage binds embankment rocks.
Description: Slender climbing or scrambling shrub with small opposite ovate-lanceolate glossy leaves and solitary or clustered sweet-scented white starry flowers.

Habitat: Large flowering avenue and shade tree
Ecological Role: Spreading umbrella-canopy tree with feathery bipinnate leaves and fiery scarlet blooms. Major shade provider, microclimate moderator, and avian nesting canopy.
Description: Magnificent broad-crowned tree producing sensational clusters of 4 spreading scarlet petals and a fifth upright variegated yellow/white standard petal.

Habitat: Moist garden bed & landscaped lawn contours
Ecological Role: Large bulbous plant bearing fragrant white spidery flowers with reddish-purple filaments. Attracts night-flying sphinx moths; roots bind loose sandy-loam soils.
Description: Massive perennial herb with thick false stems, broad strap-like fleshy leaves, and an elevated umbel of tubular pure white flowers with thread-like recurved petals.

Habitat: Large shade tree in open lawn campus groves
Ecological Role: Native nitrogen-fixing leguminous tree with fragrant puff-like greenish-yellow pompon blossoms and rattling straw-colored seed pods. Major nesting site for babblers and coucals.
Description: Large spreading tree with bipinnate leaves, mimosa-like fragrant pompon flowers with long exerted stamens, and conspicuous flat papery seed pods ('Woman's tongue tree').

Habitat: Bare soil borders, kerbside planter beds
Ecological Role: Tufted perennial grass-like herb with green leaves banded by creamy-white margins. Forms dense soil-covering root clusters and purifies ambient air.
Description: Arching perennial herb with linear variegated striped leaves that sends out stoloniferous runners bearing small white starry flowers and miniature plantlets.

Habitat: Potted ornamental, shaded corridor
Ecological Role: Broadleaf shade-tolerant foliage plant containing microscopic calcium oxalate raphides. Excellent indoor air purifier used to beautify shaded academic building breezeways.
Description: Erect perennial with thick succulent canes and large ovate-elliptic dark green leaves heavily variegated with creamy yellow-white mottling.

Habitat: Trailing groundcover over shrubs & fence lines
Ecological Role: Vigorous vine with 5-foliolate compound leaves climbing by branched tendrils. Produces small nectar-bearing flowers that feed wasps and native bees.
Description: Perennial climbing herb in the grape family with pentafoliolate palmate leaves, forked tendrils, and small greenish-white flowers developing into dark berries.

Habitat: Shaded, constantly moist rock and masonry surfaces
Ecological Role: Pioneer non-vascular plant forming spongy velvety green carpets on damp masonry and well rims. Retains atmospheric moisture, prevents erosion, and creates micro-soil for micro-arthropods.
Description: Dense cushions of miniature green gametophytes with microphyll leaves lacking vascular bundles, anchored to masonry by multicellular rhizoids.

Common Name: Pink Trumpet Tree / Rosy Trumpet Tree
Habitat: Landscaped avenues and open, sunny spaces
Ecological Role: Medium to large deciduous tree bearing showy pale-pink to lilac trumpet blossoms in dense corymbose clusters, offering a massive seasonal nectar flush for bees, butterflies, and sunbirds.
Description: Medium to large tree with palmately compound leaves and showy pale-pink to lilac, trumpet-shaped flowers borne in dense clusters, often while the crown is nearly leafless. Native to Central America and northern South America and widely planted as an ornamental avenue tree.

Habitat: Open landscaped lawns and moist soil edges
Ecological Role: Distinctive spreading tree bearing nocturnal maroon-red cup-shaped flowers pollinated primarily by fruit bats, followed by massive woody pendulum-suspended sausage-like fruits.
Description: Stout tree with rough grey bark, pinnate leaves, and nocturnal maroon cup-shaped flowers hanging on long rope-like peduncles. The heavy, gourd-like fibrous fruits hang suspended beneath the spreading canopy.

Habitat: Open campus boundary, deep soil with ample canopy space
Ecological Role: National Tree of India and ecological keystone species. Its massive spreading canopy and aerial prop roots support hundreds of birds, fruit bats, squirrels, and insects with year-round fig crops.
Description: Massive evergreen tree producing copious aerial prop roots that drop to the ground and form secondary woody trunks. Thick leathery ovate leaves with prominent pale veins and paired sessile red figs.

Habitat: Moist, acidic soil under partial canopy shade
Ecological Role: Evergreen shrub featuring serrated aromatic leaves and white nodding flowers with rich yellow stamens. Supports solitary bees and micro-pollinators.
Description: Small evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green elliptic serrated leaves and fragrant solitary white flowers with central bunches of golden-yellow stamens.

Common Name: Cathedral Bells / Air Plant / Miracle Leaf
Habitat: Dry rocky embankments, shaded garden borders
Ecological Role: Crassulacean acid metabolism (CAM) succulent bearing crenate fleshy leaves that produce adventitious plantlets along leaf margins (vegetative propagation). Provides medicinal phytochemicals and drought-resilient microhabitat.
Description: Glabrous succulent perennial herb noted for thick, scalloped fleshy leaves capable of vegetative reproduction from leaf crenations. Known widely as the 'Miracle Leaf' or 'Air Plant'.

Common Name: Neem Tree / Indian Lilac / Margosa Tree
Habitat: Temple grounds, avenue borders, arid campus soil
Ecological Role: Revered native evergreen tree producing azadirachtin-rich foliage and bark with potent bio-pesticidal and anti-microbial properties. Provides deep cooling shade, canopy cover, and edible drupes for birds and bats.
Description: Large, spreading, fast-growing evergreen tree with pinnate leaves consisting of 20 to 30 falcate-serrated leaflets and fragrant white axillary panicles followed by small golden-yellow drupes.

Habitat: Open manicured grass turf and sunny garden borders
Ecological Role: Perennial taprooted herb with a basal rosette of leaves. Serves as a ground-layer primary producer, soil stabilizer, and nectar source for micro-insects.
Description: Herbaceous perennial characterized by rigid rosette leaves closely appressed to the soil and an erect, dichotomously branched flowering stem bearing pale violet flower heads.

Habitat: Ground herbaceous layer & seed pods
Ecological Role: Red and black aposematic (warning) coloration signaling distastefulness to predators. Feeds on plant seeds and sap across composite weeds.
Description: Seed bug displaying high-contrast crimson and black geometric markings. Feeds selectively on seed fluids and serves as prey for specialized predators.

Habitat: Terrestrial & Aerial (Flowering gardens)
Ecological Role: Schedule I protected species endemic to South Asia. Striking black swallowtail with prominent crimson-red crescent spots on hindwings. Vital pollinator.
Description: Large, breathtaking swallowtail butterfly with velvety-black forewings crossed by white bands and brilliant crimson-red spots along the scalloped margin of hindwings. Pollinates diverse flowering flora.

Common Name: Indian Paper Wasp / Yellow Paper Wasp
Habitat: Terrestrial & Arboreal (Under leaf surfaces, building eaves)
Ecological Role: Primitively eusocial wasp constructing small open paper comb nests. Essential natural pest control agent preying on garden caterpillars and insect larvae.
Description: Slender brownish-yellow social wasp renowned as a model organism in sociobiology. Workers forage tirelessly for caterpillars and insect larvae to feed developing broods, providing biocontrol.

Habitat: Moist soil litter & shaded garden beds
Ecological Role: Large herbivorous land snail with conical banded shell. Acts as a decomposer of decaying plant matter, active predominantly during humid/monsoon conditions.
Description: Massive terrestrial pulmonate gastropod with a tall, conical brown and yellow variegated shell. Feeds voraciously on decaying vegetation, recycling organic matter into soil humus.

Habitat: Wetland margins, moist earthen burrows, seasonal puddles
Ecological Role: Burrowing freshwater crab active during night and rainy periods. Plays a critical role in nutrient cycling and soil aeration in campus wetland margins.
Description: Semi-terrestrial freshwater burrowing crab with dark brownish carapace and adapted chelae for digging. Deep burrows aerate soil and provide vital prey for larger wading birds and mammals.

Habitat: Foliage, flowers, and ground litter of Malvaceae plants
Ecological Role: Phytophagous bug with bright crimson body and black dorsal patches. Frequently observed in mating pairs (tail-to-tail copulation) on ground and foliage.
Description: Vibrantly colored hemipteran bug with bright red body, white transverse abdominal bands, and black markings on hemelytra. Often seen gregariously feeding on hibiscus flower buds and seeds.

Habitat: Leaf litter, decaying logs, moist soil humus
Ecological Role: Cylindrical detritivore with dark trunk and vibrant red dorsal spots/bands. Crucial primary decomposer breaking down leaf litter and enhancing soil organic matter.
Description: Striking millipede featuring a dark cylindrical exoskeleton accented by vibrant crimson-red bands and head. Plays an indispensable role in converting coarse mulch into bioavailable soil nutrients.

Habitat: Undergrowth, hedge perimeters, open ground
Ecological Role: Highly gregarious endemic passerine with a pale grey-white cap and yellowish bill. Forages in noisy groups on the ground and trees, consuming insects, berries, and nectar.
Description: Endemic southern Indian songbird renowned for foraging in tight communal flocks of 6 to 10 individuals ('Seven Sisters'). Energetically flips leaf litter to uncover hidden insects and larvae.

Habitat: High electrical lines, open canopy perches
Ecological Role: Agile insectivore with glossy black plumage and a distinct deeply forked tail. Perches high to hunt flying insects (hawking) and fearlessly mob raptors.
Description: All-black passerine with an unmistakable deeply forked tail. Renowned for its aerial acrobatic hunting displays catching dragonflies, cicadas, and moths mid-air.

Habitat: Urban / Terrestrial (Anthropogenic environments)
Ecological Role: Omnivorous, highly intelligent urban bird characterized by a grey neck collar. Functions as a scavenger cleaning food scraps and biological waste across campus.
Description: Slender crow recognized by its pale grey nape, neck, and breast contrasted with glossy black forehead and wings. Acts as a campus scavenger and opportunist predator.

Habitat: Tree canopies, building roofs, hostel terraces
Ecological Role: Endemic South Indian macaque recognized by the bonnet-like whorl of hair on its head. Plays a role in seed dispersal while foraging across fruits, leaves, and trees.
Description: Arboreal cercopithecine monkey endemic to peninsular India, noted for its radiating cap of dark hair. Troops travel across campus trees feeding on date palm drupes, peppervine berries, and tree shoots.

Habitat: Campus open grounds, shaded sandpits, shaded walkways
Trophic Level: Tertiary Consumer / Apex Predator & Scavenger (Trophic Level 4)
Ecological Role: Ancient landrace indigenous dog breed adapted to tropical climate. Highly territorial and plays a scavenger role, co-existing peacefully within the campus ecosystem.
Description: Indigenous primitive landrace dog characterized by erect ears, wedge-shaped head, and curved tail. Functions as a territorial apex mammalian scavenger across the campus boundary.

Common Name: Indian Peafowl (Peacock - National Bird of India)
Habitat: Open scrub, grassy meadows, forest edges
Ecological Role: Large ground bird with striking iridescent blue neck and fan crest. Omnivorous diet includes seeds, insects, and small reptiles (snakes), controlling garden pests.
Description: The National Bird of India, possessing iridescent cobalt blue neck plumage, fan-shaped crest, and magnificent elongated upper tail coverts with vibrant ocelli. Preys upon ground insects, snails, and lizards.

Habitat: Garden shrubs, low branches, sunny fence posts
Ecological Role: Diurnal agamid lizard capable of color change during breeding/thermoregulation. Feeds extensively on insect pests like crickets, moths, and caterpillars.
Description: Diurnal arboreal agamid lizard capable of physiological color shifts. Males develop crimson throat patches during courtship. An efficient ambush predator regulating insect pest numbers.

Habitat: Human-inhabited areas, dining halls, building perimeters
Trophic Level: Tertiary Consumer / Small Carnivore & Apex Predator (Trophic Level 4)
Ecological Role: Small carnivorous feline that controls campus rodent populations (mice, rats) around human-inhabited areas.
Description: Agile carnivorous feline adapted to semi-feral campus life. Serves as a vital biological regulator of commensal rodents and small invasive pests around student residences.

Habitat: Gardens, flowering vegetation, open areas
Ecological Role: Fast-flying tailless swallowtail with intricate yellowish-white chevron patterns on black wings and distinct tornal red eye-spots. Key pollinator of flowering campus shrubs.
Description: Prominent swallowtail butterfly displaying black wings densely patterned with sulfur-yellow markings and a blue-and-red eyespot on the inner margin of hindwings. Larvae feed on Rutaceae.

Location: Bio Block & Storm-water drain off Hostel Link Road
Habitat: Wetlands, drains, standing water and freshwater margins
Ecological Role: Semi-aquatic non-venomous colubrid snake that feeds primarily on fish, frogs, and small amphibians in campus stormwater drains, serving as a biological regulator of drain wetland fauna.
Description: Robust medium-sized freshwater snake with keeled dorsal scales and characteristic checkered black-and-olive dorsal pattern. Demonstrates exceptional diving and swimming agility.
Survey Source: Assignment 2 Survey (Team Katyayani & Team Prathin & Team Rehan)

Habitat: Semi-shaded green belt and nectar shrubbery
Ecological Role: Aposematically colored butterfly sequestering toxic cardenolides from host plants, rendering it unpalatable to predatory birds. Efficient pollinator with slow, cruising flight.
Description: Large, elegant danaid butterfly featuring blackish-brown wings with distinct bluish-white semi-transparent streaks and submarginal spots.

Location: Service road south of Hostel Link Road
Habitat: Corridor walls near outdoor nighttime illumination
Ecological Role: Nocturnally active moth attracted to exterior artificial lights, forming an essential nocturnal food base for hunting campus geckos and resting garden lizards.
Description: Cryptically camouflaged stout-bodied moth with drab greyish-brown forewings held roof-like over the body at rest.

Location: Near Cricket Ground & Main Canteen lawns
Habitat: Open grassy patches with low flowering herbs
Ecological Role: Hardy aposematic butterfly that exhibits unpalatability to predators by secreting foul fluids from legs. Pollinates ground composites (Tridax, Persicaria).
Description: Small-to-medium butterfly with translucent tawny-orange wings bordered by a black margin embedded with white spots and black transverse spots on forewings.

Habitat: Building ledges, low dense shrubbery, gregarious flocks
Ecological Role: Congeneric cousin to the Yellow-billed Babbler, distinguished by its uniformly mottled earthy-grey plumage and faint streaking. Forages in noisy cooperative groups, aerating leaf litter and gleaning insect pests.
Description: Medium-sized brownish-grey songbird with pale creamy eyes, heavy yellow bill, and mottled upperparts. Travels in close-knit groups through lower vegetation.

Habitat: Open grassland, dry twigs near marshy terrain
Ecological Role: Distinctive slender dragonfly characterized by exceptionally long legs adapted to perch on bare emergent twigs facing windward. Voracious predator of mosquitoes, gnats, and flies.
Description: Medium dragonfly with yellowish-brown thorax, black-and-yellow patterned abdomen, red pterostigma, and noticeably elongated legs used to perch prominently on dry stalks.

Habitat: Sunny pavement, masonry bases, leaf litter near trees
Ecological Role: Aposematic hemipteran that feeds on fallen tree seeds (especially Sterculiaceae & Malvaceae), aggregating in large gregarious clusters on sunlit pavements.
Description: Stout shield-shaped bug with vivid orange-red thorax and hemelytra marked with distinct black central rhomboid patches. Distinct from Dysdercus cingulatus.

Habitat: Foraging across Ixora and Hibiscus floral beds
Trophic Level: Primary Consumer / Kept & Wild Pollinator (Trophic Level 2)
Ecological Role: Indigenous wild social honeybee vital for campus cross-pollination. Forages extensively on tubular Ixora flowers, transferring pollen across flora.
Description: Medium-sized honeybee with golden-yellow and dark brown abdominal stripes, hairy thorax, and specialized pollen baskets (corbiculae) on hind legs.

Habitat: Dense tree canopy, campus grove, tangled thickets
Ecological Role: Large non-parasitic cuckoo that stalks ground and lower branches hunting snakes (including keelbacks), lizards, large beetles, snails, and caterpillars. Acts as a top avian regulator.
Description: Striking large glossy-black bird with contrasting deep chestnut-rufous wings and ruby-red eyes. Renowned for its deep resonant 'coop-coop-coop' territorial call.

Habitat: Flowering hedges, open sunny garden beds
Ecological Role: Classic Batesian mimic butterfly whose females mimic unpalatable species like the Crimson Rose. Larvae graze on Rutaceae plants while adults are active pollinators.
Description: Jet-black swallowtail butterfly; males display a distinct band of white discal spots across the hindwing, while females display polymorphic Batesian mimicry morphs.

Location: Vama Sundari Park & Dry Scrub Paths
Habitat: Ground surface, sandy soil, and dry leaf litter
Ecological Role: Fierce cursorial ground predator hunting ants, caterpillars, and soft-bodied insects. Defends itself by spraying irritating formic acid when threatened.
Description: Large, flightless ground beetle with a velvety black body ornamented with six conspicuous creamy-white dorsal spots (four on elytra, two on thorax).

Habitat: Dense foliage, tall grasses, and shrub crowns
Ecological Role: Leaf-mimicking nocturnal herbivore that feeds on foliage, flowers, and buds. Serves as key prey for lizards, praying mantises, and birds.
Description: Bright green cricket with exceptionally long, hair-like antennae exceeding body length and leaf-shaped wings that provide camouflage among foliage.

Habitat: Stagnant water pools, drainage channels, shaded corridors
Ecological Role: Aquatic larvae filter organic particulate matter in standing pools; adults feed on plant nectar (males) or vertebrate blood (females), serving as critical prey for dragonflies and bats.
Description: Slender, long-legged insect with piercing-sucking proboscis and scaled wing veins. Rests with thorax and abdomen held parallel to the resting surface.

Common Name: Common Picture Wing Dragonfly / Variegated Flutterer
Habitat: Open airspace near ponds, drainage basins, and marshy lawns
Ecological Role: Distinctive fluttering dragonfly with butterfly-like flapping flight. An agile aerial insectivore preying on gnats, midges, and mosquitoes over campus water bodies.
Description: Striking dragonfly with golden-amber and iridescent dark purplish-brown mottled wings resembling butterfly wings. Flutters gently above water margins.

Location: Foliage of Mango and Guava Trees
Habitat: Leaves and twigs of bushes inhabited by Asian weaver ants
Ecological Role: Extraordinary Batesian and aggressive mimic that perfectly resembles aggressive weaver ants (*Oecophylla smaragdina*) to deter predators while hunting small insects.
Description: Slender jumping spider with an elongated abdomen and waist-like cephalic constrictions mimicking an ant body. Males possess elongated forward-pointing chelicerae.

Habitat: Shrub leaves, tree bark, sunny foliage
Ecological Role: Diurnal visual hunter with acute stereoscopic vision that stalks and pounces on flies, leafhoppers, and small garden insects without building silk webs.
Description: Slender, colorful salticid spider; females exhibit a yellowish-green body with two prominent longitudinal reddish-brown stripes along the opisthosoma.

Habitat: Damp leaf litter, garden soil, drain margins, nocturnal walkways
Ecological Role: Nocturnal terrestrial amphibian consuming large numbers of insects, termites, and snails. Features prominent parotoid glands secreting protective bufotoxins.
Description: Medium to large stout-bodied toad with rough, warty skin accented by black-tipped spines and elevated cranial ridges. Active primarily at dusk and during humid weather.

Common Name: Indian Cricket Frog / Wetland Paddy Frog
Habitat: Moist grass, seasonal puddles, edges of drainage ditches
Ecological Role: Small, moisture-dependent frog that feeds voraciously on aquatic and semi-terrestrial insect larvae. Serves as primary prey for water snakes and egrets.
Description: Small cryptic frog with longitudinal glandular ridges along its greyish-brown dorsum and pointed snout. Renowned for its rapid, repeating cricket-like advertisement calls.

Common Name: Peninsular Rock Agama / South Indian Rock Agama
Habitat: Rocky outcrops, granite landscaping blocks, brick walls
Ecological Role: Heliothermic saxicolous lizard that basks on rocks to thermoregulate while ambushing ants, beetles, and crickets. Dominant breeding males display bright orange-and-black coloration.
Description: Flattened rock-dwelling agamid with a triangular head and keeled scales. Breeding males exhibit brilliant orange or crimson head and back contrasted with jet-black sides.

Habitat: Dry scrub, grass margins, and rocky ground crevices
Ecological Role: Solitary nocturnal serpentine predator that controls rodent, frog, and lizard populations across campus peripheral scrub belts.
Description: Slender to stout-bodied serpent featuring distinct geometric chevron occipital markings and mottled dorsal patterning adapted for cryptic camouflage in leaf litter.

Habitat: Open mown lawns, sports grounds, perimeter wetlands
Ecological Role: Gregarious terrestrial heron that stalks across open lawns feeding on disturbed grasshoppers, frogs, crickets, and worms, regulating lawn pest populations.
Description: Compact white heron with a stout yellow bill, dark legs, and during breeding season, rich golden-buff plumes on the crown, neck, and back.

Common Name: Indian Palm Squirrel / Three-striped Palm Squirrel
Habitat: Tree trunks, garden walls, ground leaf litter, building eaves
Ecological Role: Highly agile diurnal arboreal squirrel that feeds on seeds, nuts, palm fruits, nectar, and small insects. Acts as an important campus seed disperser and occasional pollinator.
Description: Small bushy-tailed squirrel with three distinctive creamy-white longitudinal stripes along its grizzled greyish-brown back. Renowned for its high-pitched bird-like alarm call.

Habitat: Anthropogenic structures, temple eaves, paved courtyards
Ecological Role: Iconic urban passerine that thrives near human habitation, gleaning grass seeds and discarded food scraps while feeding insect larvae to its chicks, providing natural garden pest control.
Description: Compact, stout seed-eating passerine. Males feature a bold grey crown, chestnut neck, and black throat bib; females are soft sandy-brown with a distinct buff supercilium.

Habitat: Tree trunks, stone pavements, soil crevices near gardens
Trophic Level: Secondary Consumer / Scavenger & Generalist Predator (Trophic Level 2-3)
Ecological Role: Ubiquitous social insect that moves in erratic, rapid darting patterns ('crazy ant'). Scavenges dead invertebrates, tends aphids and scale insects for honeydew, and cleans micro-organic campus debris.
Description: Slender dark brown to black ant with extraordinarily long 12-segmented antennae and long legs, exhibiting characteristically rapid and jerky zigzag locomotion.

Location: Central Campus Grass Lawns & Dining Precincts
Habitat: Open lawns, paved walkways, outdoor canteen perimeters
Ecological Role: Highly adaptable urban passerine bird that feeds on ground insects, grasshoppers, seeds, and anthropogenic food scraps, regulating turf pest populations.
Description: Medium-sized brown starling with a black head, distinctive bright yellow orbital patch behind the eye, yellow bill, yellow legs, and white wing patches visible in flight.

Location: High Canopy Broadleaf Foliage & Neem Canopy
Habitat: Dense tree canopy, neem groves, high foliage foliage branches
Ecological Role: Arboreal frugivorous and insectivorous cuckoo that consumes figs, berries, caterpillars, and tree insects. Brood parasite primarily laying eggs in House Crow nests.
Description: Large, long-tailed cuckoo with striking sexual dimorphism. Males are glossy blue-black with a pale green bill and crimson eyes; females are dark brown spotted and barred with white.
